chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Does a believer enter the Fire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, by Allah.' I said: 'So none enters it except an unbeliever?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, except the one whom Allah wills.' So when I reiterated it upon him time and again, he said to me: 'O Zurara! I say
He (the narrator) said: 'Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hammad narrated to me from Zurara, who said: I said within myself,
ai.seo_question: Can a believer enter Hellfire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), where Imam al-Sadiq (as) balances absolute truth with divine will to avoid contradiction. Zurara’s internal critique highlights the distinction between rhetorical debate skills and profound theological wisdom, as the Imam’s simple answers were deliberate and authoritative. This dialogue underscores the Shia belief that true believers are not eternally condemned, preserving the justice of Allah while acknowledging His sovereign decree.
